title: Outgunned by feathers: the war Australia lost to a flightless bird

words.zh: 火力不如对方；被比下去
words.note: gun（枪）+ out-（胜过）。字面是“火力被压制”，也常比喻“实力不如人”：The small shop was outgunned by the supermarket chains.
words.ctx: Outgunned by feathers: the war Australia lost to a flightless bird

ex.en: The local team was [[outgunned]] from the start.
ex.zh: 本地队从一开始就实力不济。

ex.en: Small shops are often [[outgunned]] by big chains.
ex.zh: 小店常常被大型连锁店压着打。

cloze.after: by feathers: the war Australia lost to a flightless bird
cloze.szh: 败给羽毛：澳大利亚输给一种不会飞的鸟的那场“战争”

words.note: flight（飞行）+ -less（没有）。flightless birds：不会飞的鸟，如鸵鸟、企鹅、鸸鹋。
words.ctx: Outgunned by feathers: the war Australia lost to a flightless bird

ex.en: Penguins are [[flightless]] birds.
ex.zh: 企鹅是不会飞的鸟。

ex.en: New Zealand is home to several [[flightless]] species.
ex.zh: 新西兰有好几种不会飞的鸟。

words.zh: 着手、开始（做某事）；出发去
words.note: set out to do sth：带着目标开始做，常暗示后来结果不如预期：He set out to fix the car and ended up breaking it.
words.ctx: In 1932 soldiers armed with machine guns set out to rid farmland of emus.

ex.en: She [[set out to]] write a novel in a month.
ex.zh: 她着手要在一个月内写完一部小说。

ex.en: We [[set out to]] find the best pizza in town.
ex.zh: 我们出发去找城里最好吃的披萨。

words.zh: 使 A 摆脱 B、清除
words.note: rid the house of mice（把房子里的老鼠清除掉）。最常用的是 get rid of（扔掉、摆脱）。过去式和过去分词都是 rid。
words.ctx: In 1932 soldiers armed with machine guns set out to rid farmland of emus.

ex.en: We need to [[get rid of]] these old boxes.
ex.zh: 我们得把这些旧箱子扔掉。

ex.en: The new law aims to [[rid]] the streets of litter.
ex.zh: 新法律旨在清除街上的垃圾。

words.note: 表示事后才知道的结果：It turned out that he was right.（结果他是对的。）也可插在句中。
words.ctx: The birds, it turned out, had other plans.

ex.en: [[It turned out]] the shop was closed on Mondays.
ex.zh: 结果那家店周一不开门。

ex.en: The rumour, [[it turned out]], was true.
ex.zh: 结果那个传言是真的。

words.note: 常用来幽默地说“事情没按计划走”：I wanted to sleep in, but my cat had other plans.（我想睡懒觉，可我的猫另有打算。）
words.ctx: The birds, it turned out, had other plans.

ex.en: I wanted a quiet weekend, but my kids [[had other plans]].
ex.zh: 我想过个安静的周末，可孩子们另有打算。

words.note: 放在名词前：former president（前总统）、my former boss（我的前老板）。the former ... the latter：前者……后者。
words.ctx: After the First World War, thousands of former soldiers were given land in Western Australia and encouraged to grow wheat.

ex.en: She met a [[former]] classmate at the station.
ex.zh: 她在车站遇到了以前的同学。

ex.en: The building is a [[former]] factory.
ex.zh: 这栋楼以前是工厂。

cloze.before: After the First World War, thousands of

words.note: 政府给的补贴：farm subsidies（农业补贴）。动词 subsidise（补贴），形容词 subsidised（有补贴的）。
words.ctx: Times were hard: prices fell during the Depression, and the government's promised subsidies never materialised.

ex.en: Farmers rely on government [[subsidies]].
ex.zh: 农民依赖政府补贴。

ex.en: The [[subsidy]] keeps bus fares low.
ex.zh: 这笔补贴让公交票价保持在低水平。

cloze.after: never materialised.
cloze.szh: 日子很艰难：大萧条期间粮价下跌，政府承诺的补贴也一直没有兑现。

words.note: 常用否定：The promised help never materialised.（许诺的帮助始终没来。）美式拼作 materialize。
words.ctx: Times were hard: prices fell during the Depression, and the government's promised subsidies never materialised.

ex.en: The pay rise we were promised never [[materialised]].
ex.zh: 答应我们的加薪始终没兑现。

words.note: 鸟、动物季节性迁徙；人也可以：migrate to cities（迁往城市）。名词 migration。
words.ctx: Some 20,000 of them, migrating inland after the breeding season, found the farms irresistible: open water, cleared land and endless rows of crops.

ex.en: Many birds [[migrate]] south for the winter.
ex.zh: 很多鸟冬天往南迁徙。

ex.en: Young people are [[migrating]] to the cities.
ex.zh: 年轻人正在迁往城市。

cloze.after: inland after the breeding season, found the farms irresistible: open water, cleared land and endless rows of crops.
cloze.szh: 大约两万只鸸鹋在繁殖季后向内陆迁徙，发现这些农场简直无法抗拒：有水、有空地，还有一望无际的庄稼。

words.zh: 无法抗拒的、极有诱惑力的
words.note: ir-（不）+ resist（抵抗）+ -ible（能……的）。an irresistible offer / smell。

ex.en: The smell of fresh bread was [[irresistible]].
ex.zh: 新鲜面包的香味让人无法抗拒。

ex.en: They made me an [[irresistible]] offer.
ex.zh: 他们给了我一个无法拒绝的条件。

words.note: 用脚重重地踩：trample the grass / flowers。比喻“无视、践踏”：trample on sb's rights。

ex.en: The cows [[trampled]] the vegetable garden.

ex.en: Please don't [[trample]] the flowers.
ex.zh: 请不要踩踏花草。

words.note: 派人去某处：dispatch troops / an ambulance。也指寄送：dispatch an order（发货）。

ex.zh: 救护车立刻被派了过去。

ex.zh: 据某些估计，一半的店会关门。

ex.en: By conservative [[estimates]], the repairs will take a year.
ex.zh: 保守估计，维修要花一年。

cloze.before: Even by
cloze.after: estimates, each dead bird had cost around ten bullets.
cloze.szh: 即便按最宽松的估算，每打死一只鸟也要耗费大约十发子弹。

words.note: the person in charge（负责人），be in charge of sth（负责某事），take charge（接管）。
words.ctx: The officer in charge reportedly admired the emus' toughness, likening them to tanks.

ex.en: Who's [[in charge]] here?
ex.zh: 这里谁负责？

ex.en: She is [[in charge]] of the marketing team.
ex.zh: 她负责营销团队。

cloze.before: The officer in
cloze.after: reportedly admired the emus' toughness, likening them to tanks.
cloze.szh: 据说带队的军官很佩服鸸鹋的顽强，把它们比作坦克。

words.note: liken 比 compare 更书面：He likened the city to a giant maze.（他把这座城市比作一座巨大的迷宫。）
words.ctx: The officer in charge reportedly admired the emus' toughness, likening them to tanks.

ex.en: She [[likened]] the job to running a marathon.
ex.zh: 她把这份工作比作跑马拉松。

ex.en: Critics [[likened]] the film to a dream.
ex.zh: 评论家把这部电影比作一场梦。

cloze.before: The officer in charge reportedly admired the emus' toughness,
cloze.after: them to tanks.
cloze.szh: 据说带队的军官很佩服鸸鹋的顽强，把它们比作坦克。

words.zh: 使 A 与 B 对抗
words.note: pit 作动词：让双方较量。The match pits the champion against a newcomer.（这场比赛让卫冕冠军对阵新人。）
words.ctx: Yet it carries a serious lesson about pitting brute force against a problem that is really about ecology.

ex.en: The final [[pitted]] two old rivals against each other.
ex.zh: 决赛让两个老对手狭路相逢。

ex.en: The game is about [[pitting]] your wits against the computer.
ex.zh: 这个游戏就是和电脑斗智。

cloze.before: Yet it carries a serious lesson about
cloze.after: brute force against a problem that is really about ecology.
cloze.szh: 但它也有一个严肃的教训：用蛮力去对付一个本质上属于生态的问题，行不通。

words.note: brute（野兽般的）+ force（力量）。by brute force：靠蛮力。编程里 brute force 指“暴力破解”。
words.ctx: Yet it carries a serious lesson about pitting brute force against a problem that is really about ecology.

ex.en: He opened the jar by [[brute force]].
ex.zh: 他靠蛮力把罐子拧开了。

ex.en: [[Brute force]] won't solve this puzzle.
ex.zh: 蛮力解不开这道谜题。

cloze.before: Yet it carries a serious lesson about pitting
cloze.after: force against a problem that is really about ecology.
cloze.szh: 但它也有一个严肃的教训：用蛮力去对付一个本质上属于生态的问题，行不通。

words.note: a bounty on sth（对……的悬赏）。bounty hunter：赏金猎人。也表示“丰盛”：the bounty of the harvest。
words.ctx: In the end, what worked better was a bounty system and sturdier fences.

ex.en: The town offered a [[bounty]] for every rat caught.
ex.zh: 镇上每抓到一只老鼠就给赏金。

ex.en: There is a [[bounty]] on his head.
ex.zh: 有人悬赏要他的人头。

cloze.before: In the end, what worked better was a
cloze.after: system and sturdier fences.
cloze.szh: 最后，更管用的是悬赏制度和更结实的围栏。

words.note: sturdy shoes / table / fence：结实的鞋 / 桌子 / 围栏。比较级 sturdier。
words.ctx: In the end, what worked better was a bounty system and sturdier fences.

ex.en: Buy a [[sturdy]] pair of boots for the hike.
ex.zh: 买双结实的靴子去徒步。

ex.en: We need a [[sturdier]] table.
ex.zh: 我们需要一张更结实的桌子。

cloze.before: In the end, what worked better was a bounty system and
cloze.after: fences.
cloze.szh: 最后，更管用的是悬赏制度和更结实的围栏。

words.note: wander around the town（在城里闲逛）。也指思绪走神：My mind wandered.
words.ctx: Emus remain plentiful, and still wander onto farms from time to time.

ex.en: We [[wandered]] around the old town all afternoon.
ex.zh: 我们在老城区逛了一下午。

ex.en: Don't let the children [[wander]] off.
ex.zh: 别让孩子们走丢了。

cloze.before: Emus remain plentiful, and still
cloze.after: onto farms from time to time.
cloze.szh: 鸸鹋至今数量众多，时不时还会溜达到农场里。

words.note: be said to do：据说（现在）……；be said to have done：据说（以前）做过……。The castle is said to be haunted.（据说城堡闹鬼。）He is said to have met the Queen.（据说他见过女王。）
words.ctx: Australia, meanwhile, has learnt to laugh about the only war it is said to have lost to a bird.

ex.en: The house [[is said to have]] belonged to a famous painter.
ex.zh: 据说这栋房子曾属于一位著名画家。

ex.en: The lake [[is said to be]] bottomless.
ex.zh: 据说这个湖深不见底。

words.conn: 主语 + be said to do（现在）/ to have done（过去）

pick.q: The tree is said ___ over 500 years old.
pick.why: 说的是树现在的年龄，用 be said to be。

pick.q: Shakespeare is said ___ in this inn.
pick.why: 说的是过去的事（莎士比亚曾住过），用 to have done。

cloze.before: Australia, meanwhile, has learnt to laugh about the only war it is
cloze.after: to have lost to a bird.
cloze.szh: 与此同时，澳大利亚也学会了拿这场据说是唯一一场输给鸟的“战争”开玩笑。

words.note: characteristic（特点）+ -ally。表示“正如其一贯作风”：He was, characteristically, late.（他一如既往地迟到了。）
words.ctx: The emus, characteristically, have declined to comment.

ex.en: She replied, [[characteristically]], with a joke.
ex.zh: 她一如既往地用一个笑话作答。

ex.en: The weather was [[characteristically]] grey.
ex.zh: 天气一如既往地灰蒙蒙的。

cloze.before: The emus,
cloze.after: , have declined to comment.
cloze.szh: 鸸鹋们一如既往地拒绝发表评论。
